What does a bank debit memorandum generally tell the depositor?
The account balance was decreased
The account balance was increased
A check has not yet been presented
A deposit is in transit
To the bank, your deposit is a liability; a debit reduces it. Examples: NSF checks, service charges.

What does a bank credit memorandum generally tell the depositor?
The account balance was increased
The account balance was decreased
The company made an error
A check bounced
A credit increases the bank's liability to you. Examples: interest, collections.

Outstanding checks are checks that have been:
Written, recorded and sent to payees, but not yet paid by the bank
Paid by the bank but not recorded by the company
Written but not yet recorded
Returned for insufficient funds
They reduce the company's books but not yet the bank's balance, so they are deducted from the bank balance.

A deposit in transit is a deposit that:
Has been recorded by the company but not yet by the bank
Has been recorded by the bank but not by the company
Was returned NSF
Was made by the bank on the company's behalf
